CONFIDENCE WARNING. Two inputs that drive every per-share figure are unsourced estimates: shares outstanding (~362m, derived from the pre-Calpine count plus stock consideration) and net debt (~USD 30bn post-Calpine). A 15% error in either moves fair value by more than the gap to the market price. This dossier's confidence is materially lower than the Apple or Mastercard equivalents and the rating reflects that.

findings.claim: The asset base is genuinely irreplaceable: the largest US nuclear fleet, now combined with Calpine's dispatchable gas capacity. New nuclear cannot be permitted and built on any timescale relevant to current demand.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the fleet composition and nuclear build timelines

findings.claim: Operating performance is excellent. Nuclear capacity factor was 93.0% for the owned fleet in Q2 2026, across 106 total outage days including 86 planned refuelling days over six outages.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Capacity growth comes from uprates rather than new build — the Walmart PPA enables a 30 MW expansion at Dresden. Uprates are cheap megawatts but they are incremental, not transformational.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The bottleneck is physical and favours the incumbent: no new nuclear capacity can enter this market for a decade or more, which is the structural reason the contracted premium exists and should persist.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Constellation agreed to sell the Brazos Valley Energy Center, a 606 MW ERCOT gas plant, for USD 860m before adjustments — the last asset sale required under the Calpine regulatory commitments.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Nuclear is capital-intensive in a way the thesis does not address: refuelling outages, licence renewals and life-extension capital are permanent, large and non-discretionary. Six outages in a single quarter is the normal cost of running this fleet.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

risks.text: Nuclear refuelling, licence renewal and life-extension capital are permanent and non-discretionary, and the free cash flow conversion cannot be assessed without them.
An operational event at a single large unit is a material earnings event; six outages a quarter is normal, an unplanned extended outage is not.

catalysts.text: Completion of the Brazos Valley divestiture
Further uprate announcements tied to PPAs

conclusions: The asset base has the strongest entry barrier in this batch: no competitor can build the primary asset at all on any relevant timescale.
Operating execution is excellent — a 93.0% nuclear capacity factor across six outages including 86 planned refuelling days.
Growth comes from uprates, which are cheap megawatts but incremental. The 30 MW at Dresden is representative in scale.
The cost the thesis omits: nuclear refuelling, licence renewal and life-extension capital are permanent, large and non-discretionary, and they determine how much EBITDA becomes free cash flow.
thesisImpact: Phase 2 confirms an exceptional and irreplaceable asset base while identifying the disclosure that Phase 5 most needs: sustaining capital expenditure. A nuclear fleet's EBITDA and its free cash flow are further apart than in almost any other asset class.
